creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 7 item 3, batch 9 item 3, and batch 14 echo 1.

A script that contains any prompt is refused up front by RAD20046 when there is no terminal. The remedy is `--reply`/`--reply-na`, but `@enable_global_options = 0` removes those flags, so such a script cannot run from CI, cron or an agent at all, even on runs that never reach the prompt:

```rad
---
@enable_global_options = 0
---
args:
    hint str = ""
if hint == "exact":
    print("resolved without prompting")
else:
    print(pick(["a", "b"]))
```

```
$ rad wrapper.rad exact </dev/null
error[RAD20046]: this script needs to ask you something, but there's no terminal
  ... it sets @enable_global_options = false. That removes the --reply flag ...
```

The two settings serve unrelated goals: the macro shapes the CLI a wrapper presents (passthrough wrappers set it so the wrapped tool's `-h`/`-d`/`-q` reach it), while `--reply` supplies input a terminal would otherwise give. The suggested fix, re-enabling global options, gives up what the macro was set for. Batch 9 split its pickers into a separate helper script to work around it.

Batch 9 adds a second cost of the up-front check for scripts that do have globals: a run that provably never prompts still needs `--reply-na <line>`, and the line number drifts with every edit (one wrapper's agent calls all carry `--reply-na 165`).

Options raised: keep `--reply`/`--reply-na` (and maybe `--help`) when global options are disabled; defer the terminal check to the prompt site (fail there, RAD20047 style); or a macro opting a script out of the preflight.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1); RAD20046's doc describes this as intended.

Where: core/preflight.go.

### Batch 14, echo 1

RAD20046 refuses to start a script that contains a prompt when there is no terminal, even on a run that never reaches it. The only escapes are `--reply <line>:<value>` or `--reply-na <line>`, keyed by a line number that moves with the next edit. A script cannot tell the preflight that a prompt is guarded.

```rad
args:
    yes bool
    name str = ""
if not yes:
    name = input("Name? ")
```

```
$ rad setup.rad --yes --name bob </dev/null
error[RAD20046]: this script needs to ask you something, but there's no terminal
```

Reproduces on main (exit 7). Two scripts hit it: a setup command whose `--yes` plus answer flags keep `input()` unreachable, and (batch 9) a wrapper whose agent invocations all carry `--reply-na 165`. A script with `@enable_global_options = 0` has neither flag and cannot run headless at all. The setup script's author worked around it by reading `/dev/tty` through a shell command, which the preflight cannot see, giving up both `input()` and the check.

Options from the reports: a per-call headless answer (`input(prompt, headless="")`), honoring `default=` when there is no terminal, a macro opting a script out of the preflight, or deferring the terminal check to the prompt site. Any of these lets the preflight count the site as answered.

Where: `core/preflight.go:20-29` (states why the check runs up front), `core/error_docs/20046.md`.
title: The prompt preflight refuses headless runs that never reach a prompt, with no escape when global options are off
